title: Python CRUD service with enterprise-style layering
task: Review a small Python CRUD service that proposes entity/repository/service/use-case/factory/adapter layers for simple database operations.
context: The codebase is Python with FastAPI.
The service performs straightforward CRUD and validation.
There are no complex domain invariants.
The proposed layers mostly forward arguments unchanged.
evidence: Repository and service methods are one-line pass-through wrappers.
Business rules are limited to schema validation and authorization checks at boundaries.
Call stacks become longer without isolating a volatile dependency.
snippet: route -> use_case -> service -> repository -> adapter -> database
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep every layer because enterprise architecture is safer.
Introduce DDD aggregates despite the absence of invariant-heavy domain logic.
Add abstract repositories for hypothetical future databases.
expected_decision_properties: Recommend collapsing pass-through layers while preserving meaningful boundaries.
Keep external validation/auth and persistence boundaries explicit where they carry real responsibility.
Avoid forcing DDD or enterprise layering onto simple CRUD.
Prefer simple explicit Python modules/functions/classes consistent with repository conventions.
unacceptable_reasoning: Every FastAPI project should use repository and use-case patterns.
DDD should be applied to all CRUD services.
verification_expectations: Run Python tests and type checks used by the project.
Verify HTTP behavior and persistence behavior remain unchanged.
Confirm authorization/validation boundaries are not collapsed accidentally.
revisit_when: Domain invariants become complex enough to justify a richer model.
A second persistence/provider implementation creates a real substitution boundary.
Independent lifecycle ownership emerges between layers.
